notes: Account evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for regulated customer data processing (payments, KYC docs).
Strong bias to Private deployment — cannot use hosted API for PII-sensitive workflows; legal requires a dedicated control plane and explicit data residency in us-east-1.
Security team: heavy on SAML/SCIM, RBAC enforcement, KMS BYOK, audit trails integrated into Splunk/CloudTrail.
Procurement/Legal asked for SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence, encryption-in-transit + at-rest details, and a three-year log retention SLA for audit logs.
Quoted: 30-day POC inside customer VPC. POC scope: chat support-agent (sync+streaming), secure-doc-search embeddings index, reranking for fraud signals at 100 TPS sustained bursts.
They want role mapping in Console: map Okta groups -> Redwood roles (Admin, Operator, Developer, Viewer). Strict policy: Developers must not be able to modify KMS key bindings or export logs.
SSO details requested: SP-initiated SAML flow; customer will provide IdP metadata (Okta). Need Redwood SP entity ID, ACS URL, and attribute mappings (email, groups, name).
SCIM: auto-provisioning required for groups and deprovisioning. Customer asked for SCIM 2.0 bearer token lifecycle guidance and event latency expectations (<= 60s to reflect group changes).
KMS Integration: AWS KMS BYOK expected. Customer will provide KMS key ARN in us-east-1. Requirement: Redwood must support CMKs with key rotation and show logs for key usage in CloudTrail.

Audit Logging: all inference requests + policy decisions should be forwarded to customer's Splunk via syslog endpoint; control plane audit events to CloudTrail-like export. They want a demo of end-to-end log flow during POC.

Data residency: raw request/response payloads must remain in customer's VPC and be stored only in region us-east-1. Metadata for billing may be allowed to transit but must be anonymized; legal to confirm.

Quality / fallback: want automatic fallback to a quantized RD model in the same VPC if primary instance pool is saturated. Tolerance: 100–150ms added latency acceptable for fallback for non-critical workloads.

POC success metrics: 95th percentile latency <= 180ms for chat paths under 50 concurrent users, embedding throughput 200 qps with batching, and SSO/SCIM provisioning validated against 5 test accounts.
From call: 'We need tight control over KMS keys — rotate quarterly, and we need proof that keys never leave our account' (security lead — paraphrased).
Legal asked to see Redwood's DPA + KMS BYOK appendix; Diego to attach to drive and send to legal team (action item).

requirements_summary: Private VPC deployment with customer-managed control plane access and console RBAC enforced via SSO (SAML).
SCIM provisioning for users/groups; low-latency group sync <=60s preferred.
BYOK via AWS KMS (us-east-1); proofs of key usage logs and rotation policy required.
Audit logging forwarded to customer's Splunk syslog endpoint and retained for 3 years; control-plane audit exports to customer's compliance storage.
Data residency: inference payloads and KV caches must remain inside customer's VPC/region; no replication outside us-east-1 without explicit consent.
RBAC roles: Admin, Operator, Developer, Viewer with tight permission boundaries (no key export by Developer role).
POC metrics: latency and throughput SLOs (95p latency <=180ms for chat under stated load; embeddings throughput >=200 qps).
